answer: Delayed seed reveal assigns each identity a slot derived from a future beacon value, like a marble drawn only after registration closes. An agent must commit compute before the beacon’s river of entropy is public, so mass-registering identities means paying for work that may land in useless slots. Post-reveal, a plume of audit challenges targets identities whose slot assignments cluster suspiciously. Each failed challenge costs the operator a fresh hardware attestation plus lost compute, scaling linearly with fake identity count.
